Course Content Management: Anyone can view a lesson's detail — content, questions, and estimated time — without logging in.
column3:
1. Identify a lesson that belongs to a published course.
2. Discard any Authorization token.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/lessons/{id}.
4. Inspect the response body's content, questions[], and estimatedTime fields, and confirm isCompleted=false.
column4: 1. 200 OK; LessonDetailDTO returned (content, questions[], estimatedTime, etc.); isCompleted=false since no user context.
column5: - A lesson exists.

Course Content Management: A lesson's quiz questions always include the correct-answer index in the raw response, regardless of whether the caller ever attempted the quiz (confirmed pre-attempt answer leak).
column3:
1. Identify a lesson with at least one quiz question, for a caller who has never attempted it.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/lessons/{id}.
3. Open the raw JSON response (via DevTools/Network tab, not a pretty-printed summary) and locate the questions[] array.
4. Inspect each question object for a correctIndex field.
column4: 1. Each question object includes a populated correctIndex, viewable before any quiz attempt — verify via DevTools/Network raw response body.
column5: - A lesson with ≥1 quiz question exists.

Course Content Management: Marking a lesson complete uses only the caller's JWT identity — there is no client-controlled user-id parameter (regression check for a previously-fixed identity-spoofing gap).
column3:
1. Log in as any role and identify a lesson to mark complete.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/lessons/{id}/complete?completed=true with the caller's Authorization header.
3. Send the request and confirm no userId query parameter has any effect if appended.
4. Query the LessonProgress row for the caller's own user id to confirm it was written.
column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Lesson progress updated successfully"}; the LessonProgress row is written for the CALLER's own id regardless of any extra query params supplied.
column5: - Logged in; lesson exists.

Course Content Management: Submitting any quiz attempt — even one scoring 0 — automatically marks the lesson complete as a side effect.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner on a lesson with a quiz, not yet marked complete.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/lessons/{id}/quiz-attempts with a valid body and score=0.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/lessons/{id}.
4. Inspect the isCompleted field.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: isCompleted=true for the caller, even though the quiz score was 0 — auto-complete fires on any submission regardless of score.
column5: - Logged in; lesson with a quiz exists, not previously completed.

Course Content Management: There is no cap on quiz attempts — a learner can resubmit the same lesson's quiz indefinitely.

3. Inspect each response's status and attemptNumber.
4. Confirm all three attempts are distinct rows with incrementing attempt numbers.
column4: 1. All three succeed 200 OK, each creating a new attempt with an incrementing attemptNumber — no server-side maximum-attempts enforcement.
column5: - Logged in; lesson with a quiz exists.

Course Content Management: Section/question-count listing is now gated behind MANAGE_OWN_COURSES/MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN (regression check: this authoring-surface endpoint previously had no @PreAuthorize at all; a plain LEARNER is now correctly rejected).
column3:
1. Log in as a plain LEARNER.
2. Identify a course with sections and prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/courses/{courseId}/sections.
3. Send the request; inspect the response status.
4. Log in as an eligible role (TRAINER/COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR) and repeat the same call.
column4:
1. Step 3: 403 Forbidden for the LEARNER — @PreAuthorize now requires MANAGE_OWN_COURSES or MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK or MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES or ADMINISTRATOR.
2. Step 4: 200 OK for the eligible role, returning the section list with question counts.
column5: - Logged in as LEARNER and as an eligible role; a course with sections exists.

Course Content Management: The paginated question list for a section is now gated behind MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN (regression check: this endpoint previously had no role gate, leaking every correct-answer index to any authenticated user; a plain LEARNER is now correctly rejected).
column3:
1. Log in as a plain LEARNER.
2. Identify a section with questions and prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/sections/{sectionId}/questions?page=0&size=10.
3. Send the request; inspect the response status.
4. Log in as an eligible role (holding MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN) and repeat; inspect content[] for a populated correctIndex.
column4:
1. Step 3: 403 Forbidden for the LEARNER.
2. Step 4: 200 OK for the eligible role; each item in content[] includes a populated correctIndex — the answer-key exposure is now scoped to authoring roles, not any authenticated user.
column5: - Logged in as LEARNER and as an eligible role; a section with questions exists.

Course Content Management: A previously-undocumented endpoint, GET /trainer/lessons/{lessonId}/questions, is reachable by a plain LEARNER (via the LEARNER-granted ATTEMPT_QUIZ_AND_EXAM authority) and returns every quiz question's correctIndex — a second, still-open answer-key leak distinct from COURSECONTENT_FT02's lesson-detail leak, and NOT closed by COURSECONTENT_FT12's fix (that fix only locked down the section-level question list, not this lesson-level one).
column3:
1. Log in as a plain LEARNER.
2. Identify a lesson with a saved quiz (via the "Save Questions to Lesson Quiz" flow) and prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/lessons/{lessonId}/questions?page=0&size=10.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect each item in content[] for a populated correctIndex.
column4: 1. 200 OK — @PreAuthorize on this endpoint allows ATTEMPT_QUIZ_AND_EXAM, which LEARNER holds by default; each item in content[] includes a populated correctIndex, letting any LEARNER read the answer key for a lesson's quiz through this endpoint.
column5: - Logged in as LEARNER; a lesson with a saved quiz exists.

Course Content Management: Boundary values for the quantity and mode parameters either degrade gracefully or fail predictably rather than being validated.
column3:
1. Log in and prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/sections/{sectionId}/questions/select?quantity=0&mode=RANDOM; send it and inspect the result.
2. Prepare and send the same call with quantity=-1&mode=RANDOM; inspect the result.
3. Prepare and send the same call with quantity=5&mode=NOT_A_REAL_MODE; inspect the result.
4. Compare all three outcomes.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK, empty list.
2. Step 2: likely a SQL/500 error (invalid LIMIT) — confirm actual behavior.
3. Step 3: 200 OK, behaves as sequential (ORDER BY id ASC) since an unrecognized mode silently falls through to the non-random branch.
column5: - Section with questions exists.

Course Content Management: Saving a lesson's quiz question selection is a full delete-then-recreate, so submitting an empty list clears the lesson's quiz entirely rather than being rejected.
column3:
1. Save a non-empty questionIds list to a lesson's quiz via POST /api/v1/trainer/lessons/{lessonId}/questions.
2. Confirm the quiz now has that set of questions.
3. Prepare and send the same endpoint again with body {"questionIds": []}.
4. Re-fetch the lesson's quiz to confirm it is now empty.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: 200 OK {"message":"Questions saved to quiz successfully"}; the lesson's quiz now has ZERO questions — this is the documented way to clear a quiz, not an error.
column5: - Lesson with an existing saved quiz question set.

Course Content Management: Creating a single question is now gated behind MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN (regression check: this endpoint previously had no role gate at all, letting a plain LEARNER create one; a LEARNER is now correctly rejected); it remains auto-approved with zero review for whichever eligible role creates it.

2. Prepare POST /api/v1/trainer/questions body {"sectionId":<id>,"questionText":"Injected question","options":[...]}.

4. Log in as an eligible role (holding MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN) and repeat with a valid payload; query the new question's status in the database.

2. Step 4: 200 OK {"message":"Question created successfully","id":<id>} for the eligible role; the question is persisted with status="APPROVED" (hardcoded) despite zero review.

Course Content Management: Updating a question has no OWNERSHIP check — any caller holding the MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN authority (the endpoint's role gate) can edit ANY question by ID regardless of who created it, and its options are fully replaced rather than merged.
column3:
1. Log in as User B, an eligible-role user who is NOT the creator of an existing question.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/trainer/questions/{id} with new questionText/options for that question.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response and confirm the prior options were replaced entirely by the new set.
column4: 1. 200 OK; the question is updated despite B not owning it; the prior options are deleted and replaced entirely by the new set — the PreAuthorize role gate does not imply ownership scoping.
column5: - A question created by a different user exists; caller B holds an eligible authoring role (MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/ADMIN) but did not create the question.

2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/questions/group with that payload.
3. Inspect the response status/message.
4. Re-fetch the question bank / query the database to check whether the group row and the earlier successful sub-question(s) still exist.
column4:
